strapiBlog.title: Meraas Unveils a New Masterplan for Dubai Design District (d3) Expansion
strapiBlog.short_description: Dubai Design District is entering a new phase of growth following the announcement of an expanded masterplan by Meraas.

data.text:
Dubai Design District is entering a new phase of growth following the announcement of an expanded masterplan by Meraas. The revised vision reshapes the district into a creative-led waterfront neighborhood, planned as a complete urban environment rather than a standalone business zone.

Covering approximately 18 million sq. ft., the expansion introduces canal-front living, new public spaces, and pedestrian-oriented streets. The masterplan reinforces the district’s role within the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and responds to sustained demand for well-connected, design-driven urban destinations.

What is Dubai Design District - An Overview

Dubai Design District was originally established as a hub for the creative economy, supporting industries such as design, fashion, architecture, and media. Over time, it has evolved into a recognized base for global brands and regional creative businesses.

The new Dubai Design District development plan represents a shift in scale and ambition. Residential, hospitality, and lifestyle elements are being introduced alongside existing commercial and cultural uses, transforming the area into a neighborhood where people can live, work, and engage within the same setting.

Located between Downtown Dubai and Dubai Creek, d3 benefits from direct access to major business corridors while maintaining a distinct identity. This central position supports daily connectivity for residents and businesses without diluting the district’s creative focus.

The expansion also strengthens the district’s relationship with the waterfront. Visual connections to Dubai Creek and proximity to the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary introduce a natural context into the urban fabric, shaping a more balanced and long-term livable environment.

What is Included in the New Dubai Design District Development Plan?

Design Line - A Circulation Route

A central feature of the new Dubai Design District development plan is the Design Line, which forms the backbone of the expanded masterplan. Designed as a fully shaded, pedestrian-first spine, it connects the entire district while encouraging the residents and visitors to walk.

Rather than serving purely as a circulation route, the Design Line is planned as an active public realm. Art installations, landscaped areas, and community spaces are integrated along its length, supporting movement, interaction, and everyday use without reliance on cars.

Sustainability Features

Sustainability is addressed through planning and design decisions rather than isolated features. The master plan targets LEED Silver community certification, reflecting a commitment to energy efficiency, responsible construction, and long-term usability.

Walkable streets, shaded routes, and improved connectivity reduce dependence on vehicles and align with Dubai’s broader goals for healthier and more sustainable urban living.

Five Distinct Zones

The expanded district is structured around five zones, each designed to serve a distinct purpose while contributing to a cohesive whole.

Canal-front areas will introduce residential buildings and hospitality uses along a waterfront promenade. An urban core will integrate housing with curated dining and retail, embedding everyday convenience into the district. A dedicated cultural zone will center on performance venues and mid-rise residences overlooking the d3 Bowl.

Wellness-focused living will be supported through parks and sports facilities, while a creative quarter will provide galleries, studios, and loft-style spaces that reinforce the district’s creative foundation.

data.text:
Which are the Top Projects in Dubai Design District?

Recent residential launches illustrate how the expanded vision is translating into market demand. Here's a look at the most popular projects in the area.

The Edit at d3 by Meraas

The Edit is a waterfront residential development by Meraas comprising three architecturally distinct towers and 392 residences. The project offers 1 to 4-bedroom apartments and a limited number of 5-bedroom penthouses.

Atelis at Dubai Design District by Meraas

Atelis is located along the Creekside edge of Dubai Design District. The development offers 1 to 4-bedroom apartments, select sky villas, and 5-bedroom penthouses, with a strong emphasis on views, privacy, and a landscaped waterfront setting.

Design Quarter

Design Quarter is the first residential community developed within the Dubai Design District. Delivered by Meraas, the project features well-planned one and three-bedroom apartments positioned within a walkable, design-led environment at the heart of d3.

faqs.question: What is Dubai’s design district, and what is its purpose?

data.answer: Dubai Design District is a purpose-built creative hub developed to support design, fashion, art, media, and innovation-led businesses.

faqs.question: Where is Dubai Design District located?

data.answer: The district is located between Downtown Dubai and Dubai Creek, offering strong connectivity to major commercial and lifestyle areas.

faqs.question: Is Dubai Design District a free zone?

data.answer: Yes, Dubai Design District operates as a free zone, allowing full foreign ownership and a business framework tailored to creative industries.

faqs.question: What retail options are planned for Dubai Design District?

data.answer: Dubai Design District retail spaces focus on curated dining, boutique concepts, and experiential offerings integrated into the street-level environment.

faqs.question: What to do in Dubai Design District?

data.answer: d3 regularly hosts cultural events, exhibitions, performances, and waterfront experiences, with creative venues integrated throughout the district.
